描述_EN: . most of the fragments are a rich purple colour and some show the remains of green silk embroidery while others have their edges rolled over and stitched down. this shrine is one of china's great buddhist pilgrimage sites and is situated near the oasis town of dunhuang. most of the textiles from this site would have been used as banners or wrappers for religious texts. the site is part of an area of central asia we now call the silk road, a series of overland trade routes that crossed asia from china to europe. while silk textiles travelled west from china, buddhism entered china from india along this route. the victoria and albert museum has around 700 ancient and medieval textiles recovered by stein at the beginning of the 20th century. these textiles were brought back from central asia by the explorer and archaeologist sir marc aurel stein (1862-1943). the silk road was also important for the exchange of ideas. they were recovered from cave 17 of the mogao grottoes. the shrines were carved out of the gravel conglomerate naturally occurring in the region. these small fragments are of gauze weave silk.
描述_ZN: . 大部分碎片呈浓郁的紫色，一些碎片显示出绿色丝线刺绣的遗迹，另一些碎片的边缘被卷起并缝合。 该圣地是中国伟大的佛教朝圣地之一，位于敦煌绿洲镇附近。 该遗址的大部分纺织品都是作为宗教文本的旗帜或包装物。 该遗址是中亚地区的一部分，我们现在称之为丝绸之路，是一系列从中国到欧洲穿越亚洲的陆上贸易路线。 年，当丝织品从中国向西运输时，佛教也沿着这条路线从印度进入中国。 年，维多利亚和阿尔伯特博物馆有大约700件由斯坦在20世纪初找到的古代和中世纪的纺织品。 年，这些纺织品被探险家和考古学家Marc Aurel Stein先生（1862-1943）从亚洲中部带回来。 年：丝绸之路对于思想的交流也很重要。 它们是在莫高窟第17窟中发现的。 这些神龛是由该地区自然形成的砾石砾石雕刻而成的。 这些小碎片是纱织的丝绸。
